div.head: Hn mon 2.1
div.ab: Si uero non poterit illum probare, de ipso falsonario fiat iusticia mea, scilicet de dextro pugno et testiculis.
Si vero non poterit illum probare, de ipso falsonario fiat iusticia mea, scilicet de dextro pugno et testiculis.
If, however, he does not succeed in proving him guilty, justice in accordance with my laws shall be executed upon the forger himself, namely, he shall lose his right hand and suffer castration.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 284–285 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text added from Gesetze I p. 523, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

Als Fälscher gilt also auch der Verbreiter der Münzfälschung (s. d. Gl 3. 7a), der o. CHn cor 5, 1{a} zitierte expensor
The distributor of counterfeit coin (see that word in Gl 3. 7a), the expensor cited above CHn cor 5, 1{a}, therefore also counts as a counterfeiter

Statt der Hand (s. d. Gl 11) verlor der Fälscher 1108 die Augen nach Eadmer Nov. ed. Rule 193 = Flor. Wig. Pugnum erwähnt Will. Malm. zu 1107 Reg. 399, bei dem auch 411 justitiae rigor und detruncatio (V. Aldhelmi am Ende zu a. 1125) gegen Fälscher erwähnt wird. Die rihthand ward abgehauen nach Agsächs. Annalist zu 1125; wozu Parallelen bei Plummer Sax. chron. II 301; auch Ann. Margan. Daneben steht—nicht alternativ—Entmannung (s. d. Gl 3f.) laut mehrerer Quellen. In späterer Zeit liess sich der König die Verstümmelung abkaufen (nach Will. Malm.); Fälle, wo er das nicht zugab, rühmt als selbstlosen Gerechtigkeitssinn Rob. Torin. bei Freeman Nor. conq. V 841

Instead of the hand (see that word in Gl 11), the counterfeiter in 1108 lost his eyes, according to Eadmer Nov. ed. Rule 193 = Flor. Wig. Will. Malm. mentions the pugnum under 1107, Reg. 399; he also mentions, at 411, justitiae rigor and detruncatio (V. Aldhelmi at the end, under the year 1125) against counterfeiters. The rihthand was cut off according to the Anglo-Saxon annalist under 1125; for parallels to this see Plummer Sax. chron. II 301; also Ann. Margan. Alongside this—not as an alternative—castration (see that word in Gl 3f.) is attested by several sources. At a later time the king allowed the mutilation to be bought off (according to Will. Malm.); cases in which he did not permit this are praised as a selfless sense of justice by Rob. Torin. in Freeman Nor. conq. V 841
